title: salix triandra subsp. amygdalina
intro: Salix triandra subsp. amygdalina, commonly known as the white willow, is a subspecies of the Salix triandra plant, which is a type of willow tree native to Europe and Asia. The white willow has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its ability to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and lower fever. The therapeutic actions of the white willow are attributed to its anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, which are thought to be caused by the presence of salicin, a bioactive constituent that is similar to aspirin. The bioactive constituents of the white willow include salicin, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic effects and have been used to treat conditions such as arthritis, headaches, and menstrual cramps.
